entries.query: What fields does verify.sh require on every source-paths.json entry, and which ones are gated to just the git-managed or web-doc kinds?
I want to register a new documentation source in my config file — what fields am I supposed to fill in, and does it matter if I use a URL or a local folder path?
Why can't I just add a little header block to the top of a reference file the way I do in other markdown docs I've written?
When the update process finds new content, does it overwrite my current skill files right away, or does it save the changes somewhere I can look at first?
If nothing has changed upstream, does running the refresh again just take forever re-checking everything, or does it know to skip?
How would I know whether the answers I'm getting are actually backed by real source material, versus the assistant just making something up?
Of the four reference invariants, which ones does verify.sh actually check mechanically versus rely on reviewer discipline for?
Is there a size limit on how much always-on instruction text a skill can carry, and what happens if I go over it?
How does the monorepo adapter restore the Phase 1 SHA short-circuit at the slice level instead of the whole-repo level?
What are the actual files and folders that get created when I set one of these skills up?
In plain terms, what problem does this tool actually solve for our team?
What's the design rationale for goal-given delegation over a fixed pipeline, and what actually binds output quality if the model isn't following a prescribed set of steps?
Why doesn't the tool just go fetch and clone everything it finds on its own — why does it keep asking me first?
If a new version of this tool comes out, is it going to break the skill setup I already have working?
What does the apply gate actually check in REVIEW.md before it will let a staged proposal promote to the live tree?
